summaries.Romania: Romania faces energy price crisis with the highest EU increases (51.6% electricity, 9.3% gas in H1 2026), while political tensions mount over budget deficits and administrative reforms. A Chinese auto giant signals major EV infrastructure investment amid domestic economic challenges.
summaries.Healthcare: Healthcare AI deployment accelerates with new responsibility frameworks and clinical integration, while cost pressures mount on hospital systems and pharmacy benefit transparency rules take effect. Telehealth and specialized care programs expand amid shifting patient demand patterns.
summaries.Tech: Apple's product blitz continues with touchscreen MacBook Pro and iPad mini OLED launches, while AI infrastructure spending faces sustainability questions and security incidents highlight risks in crypto and cloud ecosystems. Chinese satellite AI and autonomy advances signal intensifying global AI competition.

items.title: Eurostat: România a avut cele mai mari creșteri de prețuri la electricitate și gaze din UE în prima jumătate a anului
items.snippet: Prețurile medii la energia electrică și gazele naturale plătite de gospodăriile din Uniunea Europeană au scăzut în prima jumătate a anului 2026. România a înregistrat însă cele mai mari creșteri de prețuri la electricitate și gaze dintre statele membre, potrivit datelor publicate de Eurostat. La niv
items.line: Romania's 51.6% electricity and 9.3% gas price increases in H1 2026 far exceed any other EU member, signaling systemic energy cost crisis.

items.title: Who’s responsible when clinical AI goes wrong? AMA weighs in
items.snippet: The physician association, in a new framework, outlines its views on how different parties should bear responsibility for decisions, actions and failures involving clinical AI.
items.line: AMA releases framework clarifying liability for clinical AI failures, addressing critical gap as healthcare systems deploy decision-support tools at scale.

items.title: Cracks are emerging in the AI spending boom
items.snippet: Big Tech is pouring billions into AI infrastructure, but mounting debt, negative cash flow, and growing investor skepticism are raising questions about the sustainability of the AI spending boom.
items.line: Mounting debt, negative cash flow, and investor skepticism expose cracks in Big Tech's unsustainable AI infrastructure spending boom.
